The patient’s agitation, aggression, and drug-seeking behavior suggest a hyperdopaminergic state, likely from stimulant intoxication or withdrawal, meaning there is increased dopamine in the synaptic cleft rather than decreased. None of the listed options directly describe this acute hyperdopaminergic state, but if forced to choose, decreased dopamine receptors (B) could reflect a compensatory downregulation from chronic stimulant use.
